# acceptance-criteria

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D1 Product & Requirements (PR)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Gherkin reference (Cucumber project; mirror of the official reference) — https://mirror.niser.ac.in/cran/web/packages/cucumber/vignettes/reference-gherkin.html ; Abstracta, "A Guide to Good Cucumber Practices" — https://abstracta.us/blog/testing-tools/a-guide-to-good-cucumber-practices
- **Depends on:** user-stories, requirements-writing
- **Feeds into:** user-stories, scope-control

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a story is being readied for build and its confirmation must be written; business rules (limits, seats, refunds, permissions) need scenarios that decide them explicitly, before code does.
- **Do NOT use when:** the story itself is not yet in template form (fix it in user-stories first) or the criteria would only restate the story — that is the failure this skill exists to prevent. Do not write criteria after the code to describe whatever was built.

## Rules

1. **PR-101 — Gherkin form.** Criteria are written as scenarios: Given a context, When one action or event, Then an observable outcome — in the customer's domain language.
2. **PR-102 — One behavior, one When.** Each scenario tests exactly one behavior and contains exactly one When. Two Whens means two scenarios.
3. **PR-103 — Observable Thens only.** Every Then states an outcome a test can pass or fail. Adjectives ("works correctly", "is fast", "looks fine") are rejected at review on sight.
4. **PR-104 — Failure cases are mandatory.** Every business rule named in the story gets at least one scenario, including its failure case: boundary values, empty or none cases, duplicates, and permission failures.
5. **PR-105 — Declarative, not imperative.** Scenarios state the rule that holds, not the clicks that get there. UI mechanics appear only when the mechanic itself is the rule.
6. **PR-106 — Customer language and canonical names.** Scenarios use the customer's domain terms, and entity, plan, and product names match the fact sheet exactly.
7. **PR-107 — Written before build, together.** Criteria are drafted by product, engineering, and QA together before build starts. Criteria written after the code are a defect, not documentation.
8. **PR-108 — Frozen per iteration.** Criteria are frozen once the iteration starts. A change re-opens the story for re-estimation instead of being absorbed silently.
9. **PR-109 — Executable or checklist, never dropped.** Scenarios run in the project's BDD suite where one exists. Where none exists, they run as a signed manual checklist with the same pass/fail discipline — executor and date recorded per scenario.
10. **PR-110 — Total coverage for Must stories.** Every Must-priority story in a release maps to at least one passing scenario before the release ships.
11. **PR-111 — Undefined steps fail.** A scenario referencing a step with no definition fails the suite. It is never skipped or left marked pending at release time.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PR-051 — Criteria copied from the story.** Banned: acceptance criteria that restate the story text as their own test. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: a scenario with a stated context, one action, and the observable file contents the export must produce. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-052 — Happy-path only.** Banned: a scenario set with no failure case for a rule involving limits, money, or permissions. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: add the boundary scenario at 5 of 5 and the refusal scenario at 6. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-053 — The adjective Then.** Banned: a Then clause whose assertion is an adjective or an unmeasured quality. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: "Then the results render within 2.0 seconds for a 500-row dataset, with the totals row visible above the fold." Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-054 — The unpriced money rule.** Banned: acceptance criteria for a billing story that never assert the amount charged equals the amount displayed. Defeats: DET-CON-016. Instead: the Then states the exact charge, the proration basis, and the entitlement change. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-PR-051 — BDD suite run.** Verifies: PR-110, PR-111. Check: automated — run the project's BDD suite (Cucumber or the stack's equivalent): every Must story in the release maps to at least one passing scenario, and the suite is configured to fail on undefined steps. Pass: 100% of Must stories mapped and green. Fail: block the release. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-052 — Gherkin lint.** Verifies: PR-102, PR-103. Check: automated — lint all scenario files: exactly one When per scenario; every Then contains an observable assertion (a number, a state, a message, or a file condition); adjective-only Thens are flagged from the banned-term list. Pass: zero violations. Fail: block story sign-off. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-053 — Failure-case coverage.** Verifies: PR-104. Check: manual — for each business rule in the release's stories, list its failure scenario; rules touching money, limits, or permissions must each have one. Pass: 100% of such rules covered. Fail: block build start for the uncovered story. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-054 — Checklist degradation check.** Verifies: PR-109. Check: manual — for projects with no BDD runner, confirm the signed checklist exists, names an executor and a date per scenario, and records pass or fail per scenario for this release. Pass: a complete checklist covers every scenario in the release. Fail: block the release. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Given, When, Then — one When, one behavior.
- If a test cannot fail it, the Then is wrong.
- Every rule gets its failure case.
- Behavior, not buttons.
- Criteria are written before build and frozen for the iteration.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every scenario has exactly one When (G-PR-052).
- [ ] Every Then asserts an observable outcome (PR-103).
- [ ] Every money, limit, or permission rule has a failure scenario (G-PR-053).
- [ ] Criteria were drafted before build, with product, engineering, and QA (PR-107).
- [ ] The BDD suite is green with zero undefined or pending steps (G-PR-051), or the signed checklist is complete (G-PR-054).
- [ ] Every Must story in the release maps to a passing scenario (PR-110).
- [ ] Entity and plan names match the fact sheet exactly (PR-106).

<!-- generated from skills/product-requirements/competitive-analysis/SKILL.md (bundle form) -->

# competitive-analysis

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D1 Product & Requirements (PR)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://www.nngroup.com/articles/competitive-usability-evaluations/
- **Depends on:** user-research, fact-sheet
- **Feeds into:** pricing-monetization, requirements-writing, roadmapping

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** positioning a product, deciding build/skip on a feature a competitor has, preparing differentiation claims for copy, or capturing competitor pricing as an input to pricing decisions.
- **Do NOT use when:** the question is what users need (use user-research and discovery), or the output would be a feature checklist with no decisions attached — that is unfinished work under this skill, not a deliverable.

## Rules

1. **PR-161 — Named comparison set.** The analysis names 2–4 direct competitors plus the relevant indirect alternatives, including "do nothing" / the current workaround the customer uses today.
2. **PR-162 — Same tasks, hands-on.** The same core tasks are run in each product using trial or real accounts. A capability is recorded as present only when the analyst performed it or saw it performed.
3. **PR-163 — Every cell is dated evidence.** Every cell of the comparison matrix carries a date and an evidence link (screenshot, note file, or trial record). A cell without both is empty, whatever text it contains.
4. **PR-164 — Unverified means labeled unverified.** A feature known only from a competitor's marketing page is recorded as "claimed, unverified" and is never used as the basis for a build decision or a differentiation claim.
5. **PR-165 — Pricing from the source.** Competitor prices are captured from the actual pricing page or trial checkout, with the capture date, and handed to the fact sheet. Prices are never re-typed from memory, screenshots of screenshots, or third-party roundup articles.
6. **PR-166 — Shared scoring criteria.** Products are scored against the same criteria for every row: capability coverage, usability on the task, price as actually charged, and proof offered. Criteria are fixed before scoring starts.
7. **PR-167 — Analysis ends in decisions.** The document closes with recorded decisions — build / skip / position against — each citing the matrix cells it rests on. A matrix with no decisions section is unfinished.
8. **PR-168 — Differentiation names its set.** Any differentiation claim states the comparison set it was measured against ("of the three tools trialed on 2026-11-10…"). A claim with no named set does not leave this document.
9. **PR-169 — Refresh interval is stated.** The matrix carries a refresh date. Cells older than the refresh interval are expired and cannot support new claims or decisions until re-verified.
10. **PR-170 — Conclusions cite cells.** Every conclusion (table stakes, gap, differentiation) cites the specific matrix cells behind it, so a reviewer can re-run the evidence without redoing the analysis.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PR-081 — Marketing-page matrix.** Banned: filling a comparison matrix from competitors' marketing pages without running the tasks hands-on. Defeats: DET-CON-026. Instead: verify hands-on or mark the cell "claimed, unverified" (PR-164). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-082 — Setless superlative.** Banned: a differentiation claim of the form "#1", "best", "leading", or "fastest" with no named comparison set, criteria, or date. Defeats: DET-CON-026. Instead: name the set and criteria, or rewrite as a plain description of what the product does (PR-168). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-083 — Unsourced competitor numbers.** Banned: quoting a competitor's user count, rating, or market figure in the analysis or in copy without a source the reader can check. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: cite the source and its nature ("per Y's homepage, 2026-11-21"), or drop the number. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-084 — Memory-typed competitor prices.** Banned: entering a competitor's price into the matrix, the fact sheet, or a pricing decision from memory or from a roundup article instead of the live pricing page or checkout. Defeats: DET-CON-016. Instead: capture from the source with a date (PR-165). Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-PR-081 — Evidence coverage scan.** Verifies: PR-163. Check (automated): export the matrix to CSV and run `awk -F, '$4=="" || $5=="" {n++} END {print n+0}' matrix.csv` (columns 4–5: evidence link, date). Pass: output is 0 — 100% of filled cells carry a dated evidence link. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-082 — Freshness check.** Verifies: PR-169. Check (automated): `grep -i "refresh" analysis.md` shows a stated refresh interval, and no cell date in the matrix export is older than that interval relative to today. Pass: zero expired cells in use. Fail: warn; expired cells are re-verified or struck before the analysis supports new decisions. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-083 — Decisions-present check.** Verifies: PR-167, PR-170. Check (automated): `grep -ciE "decision|build:|skip:|position" analysis.md` returns at least one decision entry. Pass: decisions section present. Fail: block shipment — the analysis is unfinished. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-084 — Hands-on sample audit.** Verifies: PR-162, PR-164, PR-167, PR-170. Check (manual): pick three cells marked verified; the analyst's trial notes or screenshots must show the task being performed. Any cell that cannot be evidenced is relabeled "claimed, unverified". Also verify that each decision line in the decisions section cites at least one cell reference; a decision with no cell citation is unfinished. Pass: all three sampled cells evidenced and every decision line carries a cell citation. Fail: warn and relabel before use. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- A competitor's marketing page is a claim, not evidence.
- Every cell: a date and an evidence link, or it is empty.
- Pricing comes from the pricing page, never from memory.
- Differentiation names its comparison set or it is cut.
- A matrix with no decisions is unfinished.

## Checklist

- [ ] Comparison set named: 2–4 direct competitors plus indirect/do-nothing (PR-161).
- [ ] Same core tasks run hands-on in each product (PR-162).
- [ ] 100% of matrix cells carry date + evidence link (PR-163, G-PR-081).
- [ ] Unverified features labeled "claimed, unverified" (PR-164).
- [ ] Competitor prices captured from live pricing pages and handed to the fact sheet (PR-165).
- [ ] Decisions section written, each decision citing matrix cells (PR-167, PR-170, G-PR-084).
- [ ] No superlative claim without a named comparison set (PR-168).
- [ ] Refresh date stated and no expired cells in use (PR-169, G-PR-082).

<!-- generated from skills/product-requirements/discovery/SKILL.md (bundle form) -->

# discovery

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D1 Product & Requirements (PR)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Torres, Opportunity Solution Tree — https://www.chameleon.io/blog/opportunity-solution-tree ; Torres, *Continuous Discovery Habits* (Product Talk Press, 2021), method summary — https://glasp.co/posts/teresa-torres-how-to-master-continuous-discovery-for-product-success-glasp-talk-31
- **Depends on:** none — standalone: discovery starts from raw customer evidence gathered directly (interviews, support tickets, usage notes the user supplies); no other skill's output is an input. Its findings feed user-research, personas-jtbd, requirements-writing, and roadmapping.
- **Feeds into:** user-research, personas-jtbd, requirements-writing, roadmapping

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a product or major feature is being shaped; the team must decide what to build next; a backlog is filling with solutions nobody has traced to a customer need.
- **Do NOT use when:** the work is a defined fix or a committed delivery item with acceptance criteria already attached — go to user-stories and acceptance-criteria instead. Do not use discovery to re-litigate a decision already recorded with its evidence.

## Rules

1. **PR-001 — One desired outcome per tree.** The Opportunity Solution Tree carries exactly one desired outcome at its root; every opportunity, solution, and assumption test hangs from that outcome.
2. **PR-002 — Opportunities are needs, not solutions.** Every opportunity node is framed as a customer need, pain, or desire in the customer's terms. A node naming a feature or build task is reclassified as a solution and moved down the tree.
3. **PR-003 — No backlog entry without an opportunity.** A solution enters the backlog only with a non-empty opportunity ID linking it to a node on the tree.
4. **PR-004 — Evidence is specific-moment stories.** Interview evidence is recorded as stories about specific past moments (who, when, what happened). Summarized opinions and feature requests are recorded as interpretation, never as evidence.
5. **PR-005 — Weekly customer touchpoints.** While the product is in active development, discovery runs at least one customer touchpoint per week; a week with none is logged as a gap in the discovery record.
6. **PR-006 — Assumption list before commitment.** Every candidate solution carries an explicit assumption list covering desirability, usability, feasibility, and viability before any build commitment is made.
7. **PR-007 — Riskiest assumption first.** Assumption tests are ordered by importance multiplied by lack of evidence; the most important, least-evidenced assumption is tested before all others.
8. **PR-008 — Target opportunity chosen by comparison.** The target opportunity is selected by comparing at least two candidate opportunities on size, frequency, and strategic fit, and the comparison is recorded on the tree.
9. **PR-009 — No test, no cycle.** A discovery cycle that produces no assumption test is incomplete and cannot close, however many interviews it ran.
10. **PR-010 — Degradation path when no customers are reachable.** When no real customers can be interviewed, evidence comes only from user-supplied material (interview notes, support tickets, analytics exports). Anything inferred beyond that material is labeled UNVERIFIED and cannot be cited by personas-jtbd or requirements-writing.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PR-001 — Solution-first backlog.** Banned: a backlog item naming a feature with no opportunity ID on the tree. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: frame the opportunity ("I need to know my ride is arriving before it reaches my stop") and attach the solution to it. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-002 — Opinion recorded as evidence.** Banned: writing summarized opinions ("users love dashboards") into the evidence record as if they were interview findings. Defeats: DET-CON-014. Instead: record the specific story ("On March 3, the dispatcher re-exported the CSV three times because totals were missing"). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-003 — Invented interview findings.** Banned: writing findings, quotes, or participant counts for interviews that never happened. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: mark the claim UNVERIFIED with no downstream citation rights, or run the interviews. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-004 — Feature-request transcription.** Banned: converting one customer's feature request directly into a backlog commitment without mapping it to an opportunity and testing its assumptions. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: place the underlying need on the tree, compare candidate solutions, and test the riskiest assumption first. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-PR-001 — Backlog opportunity lint.** Verifies: PR-003. Check: automated — run a script over the backlog export confirming every item has a non-empty `opportunity_id` field whose value exists on the tree. Pass: 100% of items carry a valid ID. Fail: block intake of the items missing IDs. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-002 — Assumption map presence.** Verifies: PR-006, PR-007. Check: manual — for the target opportunity, confirm an assumption map exists, the riskiest assumption is named, and a test is attached to it. Pass: all three present before build starts. Fail: block build start. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-003 — Evidence format audit.** Verifies: PR-004, PR-010. Check: manual — sample 5 evidence entries; each names a specific moment or carries the UNVERIFIED label with a user-supplied source. Pass: 5 of 5 conform. Fail: warn; an entry failing twice is removed from the record. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-004 — Cycle completeness.** Verifies: PR-009. Check: manual — review the cycle record for at least one assumption test whose result is written back onto the tree. Pass: test and result both present. Fail: the cycle stays open and blocks handoff to delivery planning. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- One outcome, one tree.
- Opportunities are needs; features are solutions.
- Stories about moments, not opinions.
- Test the riskiest assumption first.
- No test, no cycle.

## Checklist

- [ ] The tree root is a single desired outcome (PR-001).
- [ ] Every opportunity node is a need, not a solution (PR-002).
- [ ] Backlog lint passes: 100% of items carry a valid opportunity ID (G-PR-001).
- [ ] The target opportunity was chosen by recorded comparison (PR-008).
- [ ] The assumption map names the riskiest assumption with a test attached (G-PR-002).
- [ ] Evidence entries are specific moments or labeled UNVERIFIED (PR-004, PR-010).
- [ ] The cycle closes only with a recorded test result (PR-009).

<!-- generated from skills/product-requirements/fact-sheet/SKILL.md (bundle form) -->

# fact-sheet

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D1 Product & Requirements (PR)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Mitchell et al., "Model Cards for Model Reporting," FAT* 2019 — https://arxiv.org/html/1810.03993 ; GOV.UK publishing guidance, "Use clear language" — https://guidance.publishing.service.gov.uk/writing-to-gov-uk-standards/writing-guidelines/clear-language/
- **Depends on:** requirements-writing, competitive-analysis, pricing-monetization
- **Feeds into:** real-content, copywriting, structured-data

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** any fact about the product is about to be published anywhere — copy, pricing pages, structured data, decks, sales material — or when the single source of truth for product facts is created or re-verified. The sheet is written before any public copy.
- **Do NOT use when:** the content makes no factual claim (pure interface text, navigation labels). Do not use the sheet as a marketing document; the moment it reads like a brochure it has stopped being a fact sheet.

## Rules

1. **PR-121 — Sheet-first.** A fact enters copy, pricing pages, structured data, or sales material only after it exists in the fact sheet with its evidence. Copy is never the first place a fact appears.
2. **PR-122 — Fixed template.** The sheet uses the fixed sections: identity and provenance, intended use, inputs and dependencies, measured performance, risks, and limitations. No section is omitted. The section names come from model reporting; for a non-AI product, map the product's facts onto them instead of forcing them into model terms: identity and provenance holds the canonical product, plan, and company names (PR-129), the plan terms and prices (mirrored against billing, PR-130), and the source each fact came from; inputs and dependencies holds the data the product collects and processes, its third-party services and processors, and its billing configuration; measured performance holds the product's measured operational figures and its published limits and quotas, each with evidence (PR-123, PR-125). Where a model reading of a section does not apply — model identity under identity and provenance, training or evaluation data under inputs and dependencies — mark that reading "not applicable — non-AI product" in the sheet; the marked section satisfies G-PR-061, while an invented model fact or a plausible fill fails PR-126.
3. **PR-123 — Every number traces.** Each quantitative claim in the sheet links to the measurement, dataset, or document behind it. An untraceable number is removed, or marked UNVERIFIED in the sheet itself.
4. **PR-124 — No marketing register.** The sheet contains no superlatives and no promotional language. It reads like a lab report, not a brochure.
5. **PR-125 — Disaggregate performance.** Performance is reported broken down by the conditions that change it. An aggregate-only figure is flagged in the sheet as incomplete until the breakdown exists.
6. **PR-126 — Unknown means "not measured".** A field with no data states "not measured". A plausible fill is a fabrication.
7. **PR-127 — Owned and dated.** The sheet names an owner and a review date. A sheet past its review date blocks new claims until the owner re-verifies it.
8. **PR-128 — Limitations are mandatory.** The limitations section is non-empty for every product. A sheet claiming no limitations is rejected on sight.
9. **PR-129 — Names are canonical.** Product, plan, company, and person names appear in the sheet in their one canonical form. Every surface copies the name from the sheet, character for character.
10. **PR-130 — Prices mirror billing.** Prices and plan terms in the sheet match the billing configuration exactly. The sheet is updated in the same change as any price change — never after, never separately. Where no billing provider exists, the sheet's own price entries are the source of truth (see G-PR-063).
11. **PR-131 — One sheet per product.** All departments cite the same sheet. Private copies and per-page fact variants are merged into it or deleted.
12. **PR-132 — Changes are versioned.** Every fact change carries a date and a reason in the sheet's history, and downstream surfaces are re-checked against the new value.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PR-061 — Copy-first facts.** Banned: publishing a claim that does not exist in the fact sheet. Defeats: DET-CON-014. Instead: add the fact to the sheet with its evidence first, then publish it. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-062 — The invented statistic.** Banned: any number, in the sheet or in copy, with no measurement, dataset, or document behind it. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: measure it and cite the dataset, or delete the number. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-063 — The borrowed credential.** Banned: entering an award, certification, press mention, or partnership claim without the issuer's own confirmation. Defeats: DET-CON-012. Instead: link the issuer's or outlet's own listing, or remove the claim. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-064 — The plausible fill.** Banned: filling an unknown sheet field with a reasonable-sounding value instead of "not measured". Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: write "not measured" until instrumentation exists, then record the measured value with its source. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-065 — The brochure sheet.** Banned: superlatives or promotional claims inside the sheet itself. Defeats: DET-CON-026. Instead: state the measurable fact (customers, market, date) or state nothing. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-PR-061 — Template completeness.** Verifies: PR-122, PR-127, PR-128. Check: automated — run a script over fact-sheet.md confirming all fixed sections are present, the limitations section is non-empty, an owner is named, and the review date is in the future. Pass: all four conditions true. Fail: block new claims until the sheet is repaired. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-062 — Claim-trace audit.** Verifies: PR-121, PR-123. Check: semi-automated — extract quantitative claims from shipped copy with a script, sample 10, and resolve each against a sheet entry with an evidence link. Pass: 10 of 10 trace. Fail: one untraceable claim fails the release's content pass. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-063 — Price mirror diff.** Verifies: PR-130. Check: automated — diff the sheet's prices and plan names against the billing configuration export. Where no billing provider exists, the diff runs against the fact sheet's own price entries as the source of truth, per pricing-monetization PR-210. Pass: zero differences. Fail: block the release. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-064 — Staleness block.** Verifies: PR-127. Check: automated — compare the sheet's review date against today's date at release time. Pass: the review date is in the future. Fail: block new claims until the owner re-verifies the sheet. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Sheet first, copy second — never the reverse.
- Every number traces or it is marked UNVERIFIED.
- Unknown is written "not measured", never filled.
- No superlatives in the sheet, ever.
- One sheet, one owner, one review date.

## Checklist

- [ ] Template completeness passes: all sections, non-empty limitations, owner, future review date (G-PR-061).
- [ ] Every quantitative claim in the sheet links to evidence (PR-123).
- [ ] Performance figures are disaggregated by condition (PR-125).
- [ ] No field carries a plausible fill; unknowns say "not measured" (PR-126).
- [ ] Names match the canonical forms used on every surface (PR-129).
- [ ] Prices diff clean against the billing configuration (G-PR-063).
- [ ] The claim-trace audit sample resolved 10 of 10 (G-PR-062).
- [ ] Fact changes carry date and reason in the history (PR-132).

<!-- generated from skills/product-requirements/market-expansion/SKILL.md (bundle form) -->

# market-expansion

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D1 Product & Requirements (PR)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** World Bank Global Findex Database (payment-method and account-ownership data by economy) — https://globalfindex.worldbank.org/ ; Unicode CLDR (locale data: currencies, date/number formats, names) — https://cldr.unicode.org/ ; W3C Internationalization — https://www.w3.org/International/
- **Depends on:** competitive-analysis (local competitive set and prices), localization-workflow (locale support tiers and release sign-off), privacy-laws (obligations register for the new market), data-residency (transfer/residency verdicts), pricing-monetization, unit-economics, fact-sheet
- **Feeds into:** roadmapping, requirements-writing, scope-control

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** an existing, already-shipping product is being considered for launch into a new country or distinct market, and someone must decide go / conditional-go / no-go. This skill owns that decision: one readiness record per market, six readiness dimensions scored on evidence, pre-registered criteria, a pilot with kill thresholds, and a recorded decision a reviewer can re-run.
- **Do NOT use when:** running the translation process itself (use localization-workflow; this skill consumes its per-locale tier and sign-off, it does not redo them), determining which privacy or residency obligations apply (use privacy-laws and data-residency; this skill consumes their registers as inputs and never re-derives the law), analysing competitors as an end in itself (use competitive-analysis; this skill consumes its matrix), or launching a brand-new product with no existing market (use discovery and roadmapping — there is no home-market baseline to expand from).

## Rules

1. **PR-261 — One readiness record per market.** Each candidate market gets exactly one readiness record (file or tracker entry) that is the single artifact for the decision. It carries: market, target launch window, named decision owner, named decider, the six dimension sections of PR-264, the criteria of PR-263, the pilot plan of PR-274, and the decision of PR-262. A judgement that lives only in a meeting, a chat thread, or a slide deck does not exist as far as this skill is concerned.
2. **PR-262 — The decision is written, dated, and one of three values.** The record closes with exactly one decision — GO, CONDITIONAL GO (conditions listed, each with an owner and a date), or NO-GO (reasons listed, each citing the dimension evidence behind it) — signed by the named decider and dated. Work that spends money, signs contracts, or announces dates before this decision exists is unauthorised expansion work, whatever its intent.
3. **PR-263 — Criteria are fixed before scoring.** The pass thresholds for every dimension are written into the record before any dimension is scored. A threshold changed after its dimension was scored voids that dimension's score; the dimension is re-scored against the new threshold and both versions stay in the record. Criteria invented to fit a score already reached are not criteria.
4. **PR-264 — Six dimensions, scored separately, never averaged.** The record scores each of: (1) localization readiness, (2) payments readiness, (3) legal readiness, (4) pricing readiness, (5) support readiness, (6) cultural fit. Each dimension gets its own verdict — READY, READY WITH CONDITIONS, or BLOCKED — with its evidence. There is no overall percentage and no average: a strong dimension never compensates for a weak one in the arithmetic, only in the decider's written reasoning.
5. **PR-265 — A BLOCKED dimension blocks GO.** If any dimension is BLOCKED at decision time, the only available decisions are CONDITIONAL GO (with the unblocking work as dated conditions, and no public launch until they close) or NO-GO. A GO recorded over a BLOCKED dimension is invalid and is treated as no decision.
6. **PR-266 — Every dimension verdict cites dated evidence.** Each verdict names its evidence: a document, register row, test record, or named person's dated assessment, with the date it was produced. Evidence older than the record's review date (PR-279) is expired and cannot support a verdict. "The team is confident" is not evidence and scores nothing.
7. **PR-267 — Localization verdict is imported, not re-judged.** The localization dimension copies the locale's support tier and release sign-off from localization-workflow (full / UI-only / best-effort, reviewer sign-off per locale) for the market's primary language(s). The dimension is READY only when the tier the launch will claim publicly has actually been signed off there. This skill never upgrades a tier; a gap is recorded as a condition or a blocker, and the fix is routed back to localization-workflow.
8. **PR-268 — Payments are proven by live transactions, not by a provider logo.** The payments dimension is READY only when: the payment methods the record claims are the ones in-market users actually use (sourced — e.g. provider documentation for the market, Global Findex data, or in-market user research — never assumed from the home market); at least one real end-to-end transaction per claimed method has been executed in production or the provider's live environment, including a successful charge, a failure path, and a refund; and prices, tax, and receipts display in the market's currency and format. A method integrated in test mode only is recorded as not ready.
9. **PR-269 — Legal verdict is imported from the registers.** The legal dimension copies its inputs from privacy-laws (the obligations register rows for this market) and data-residency (transfer/residency verdicts for the infrastructure that will serve this market), plus three market-entry facts recorded with sources and dates: whether a local entity, registration, or licence is required to sell here and its status; the tax-registration position (e.g. VAT/GST or local equivalent) and its status; and any sector-specific licence or content rule that applies to this product. This skill records the status of each; it does not interpret the law. Any item whose status is "required, not obtained" makes the dimension BLOCKED. Where privacy-laws marks an escalation stop, qualified local counsel's written input is attached before the dimension can be scored at all.
10. **PR-270 — The local price is set deliberately, never converted.** The price charged in the new market is a decision recorded in the record and handed to the fact sheet: it starts from in-market evidence (competitor prices from competitive-analysis captured from live local pricing pages, willingness-to-pay evidence from in-market research) and is checked against the market-level unit economics of PR-275. A price produced by converting the home-market price at a spot exchange rate, with no local evidence step, does not satisfy this rule — see BAN-PR-132.
11. **PR-271 — Support exists before the first local user does.** The support dimension is READY only when the record names: who answers users in this market (person, team, or vendor), in which language(s), during which hours stated in the market's timezone, with what first-response target, and through which channels. Help content for the primary flows exists at the locale tier claimed under PR-267. "The home team will pick it up" with no named coverage for the market's waking hours is BLOCKED, not a condition.
12. **PR-272 — Cultural fit is reviewed by a named in-market reviewer.** A named person who lives in or is from the target market — not a home-market team member who visited — walks the primary flows and the launch copy and records every adaptation the product needs: names and imagery, forms of address, date/time/calendar conventions, units, address and phone formats, locally expected workflows (e.g. invoicing, ID, or delivery norms the product touches), and anything that would read as offensive, implausible, or foreign in a way that breaks trust. Each recorded adaptation is marked done, scheduled as a dated condition, or waived in writing by the decider with a reason. No reviewer, no dimension score.
13. **PR-273 — Demand evidence comes from the market, not from extrapolation.** The record's demand section cites evidence gathered from people in the target market — interviews, a waitlist or landing test run in-market, a pilot cohort, distributor/partner commitments in writing — each dated and counted. Home-market growth rates, home-market conversion, and total-addressable-market figures for the country are context, never demand evidence, and are labeled as context wherever they appear.
14. **PR-274 — Every GO is a pilot first.** A GO decision launches to a limited cohort or region within the market, for a stated period, with success thresholds and kill thresholds written into the record before the pilot starts (drawn from product-metrics: e.g. activation, first-transaction completion, support contacts per user, refund rate — the specific metrics are the project's, the requirement to pre-register them is this rule's). Full launch requires a post-pilot review (PR-278) against those thresholds. A pilot with no kill threshold is a launch with extra steps and does not satisfy this rule.
15. **PR-275 — Unit economics are re-derived for the market.** The record carries a market-level unit-economics check (per unit-economics) built from local inputs: local price (PR-270), the actual payment-processing cost of the methods claimed under PR-268, local support cost from the PR-271 model, local acquisition channel and cost evidence, and applicable taxes/fees. Home-market margins pasted into the new market's row are a scoring error: any input not sourced locally is flagged as an assumption, and a dimension resting on flagged assumptions cannot be READY.
16. **PR-276 — Operational prerequisites are listed and closed.** The record lists the hard prerequisites for operating in the market — app-store or distribution accounts, business/banking/tax registrations from PR-269, domain and trademark position where the product relies on them, data infrastructure region per data-residency — each with status and owner. An open prerequisite that would prevent selling, charging, or operating is a BLOCKED verdict on its dimension, not a footnote.
17. **PR-277 — The exit plan is written before entry.** The record states how the launch is paused or withdrawn: how users are told, in their language; what happens to subscriptions, balances, and prepaid amounts; what data obligations survive exit (from the privacy-laws register); and who owns the decision to exit. A market the team cannot describe leaving is not ready to enter.
18. **PR-278 — The post-pilot review is a second decision.** At the pilot's stated end date the decider records a second decision — EXPAND to full launch, HOLD (extend pilot with new dated thresholds), or EXIT (per PR-277) — citing the pilot's actual metric values against the PR-274 thresholds. Silence at the review date is a HOLD by default, never an automatic expand.
19. **PR-279 — The record expires.** The record carries a review date, set when the decision is made. After that date the record is stale: its verdicts cannot support a new launch, a new claim, or a new market's decision until the affected dimensions are re-evidenced. One market's record is never reused as another market's evidence; a shared input (e.g. the same language) is re-cited per market, not inherited.
20. **PR-280 — Public claims match the record.** Any public statement about the launch — "now available in X", "fully localized", "supports <payment method>", local pricing pages, launch dates — is checked against the record before publication: availability matches the pilot/full status, the localization claim matches the PR-267 tier, payment claims match PR-268's live-tested methods, and prices match the fact sheet. A claim the record cannot support is cut or corrected before it ships, not after users find it.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PR-131 — Invented market numbers.** Banned: stating a market size, demand figure, user count, or growth rate for the target market in the record, a pitch, or launch copy without a checkable source and date. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: cite the source and its nature ("per <source>, <date>") and label the figure context under PR-273, or leave the field empty and record demand as unknown. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-132 — FX-converted pricing.** Banned: setting the new market's price by converting the home-market price at a spot exchange rate and presenting the result as the local price. Defeats: DET-CON-016. Instead: set the price from in-market evidence and market unit economics (PR-270, PR-275) and hand the single resulting price to the fact sheet. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-133 — Announcement before backing process.** Banned: publicly announcing availability, a launch date, or "coming soon" sign-ups for a market before the decision exists (PR-262) and the support and payments dimensions are at least READY WITH CONDITIONS. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: announce only what the record supports, when it supports it (PR-280); a waitlist is announced as a waitlist. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-134 — The verbal go.** Banned: treating a meeting outcome, a chat message, or an executive's remark as the expansion decision, with no written record, criteria, or named decider. Defeats: DET-NONE — no DET parameter names this signal; governed by PR-261, PR-262, PR-263. Instead: no decision exists until the record carries the dated, signed GO / CONDITIONAL GO / NO-GO of PR-262 against the pre-registered criteria of PR-263. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-135 — Test-mode payments presented as live.** Banned: recording or claiming a payment method as supported in the new market when it has only ever run in a sandbox/test environment, or when its refund path has never been executed. Defeats: DET-FAKE-006. Instead: readiness requires a real charge, a real failure path, and a real refund in the live environment, recorded with dates (PR-268). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-136 — Readiness copy that contradicts the record.** Banned: launch copy, help pages, or sales answers that describe the market's availability, localization, or payment support at a level above what the readiness record and fact sheet state. Defeats: DET-CON-014. Instead: every public claim is checked against the record before publication (PR-280); where copy and record disagree, the record wins and the copy is corrected. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-PR-131 — Record completeness scan (automated).** Verifies: PR-261, PR-264, PR-274, PR-277, PR-279. Check: count each term separately — `for t in localization payments legal pricing support "cultural fit"; do grep -ci "$t" record.md; done` must return at least one hit for every one of the six dimensions, and the same per-term loop over `pilot "kill threshold" exit "review date" decision` must return at least one hit each for the pilot plan, kill threshold, exit plan, review date, and decision fields. A single combined `grep -c` count cannot prove per-term presence and does not satisfy this gate. Pass: all six dimension sections and all five fields present. Fail: block shipment — an incomplete record cannot be decided. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-132 — Blocker scan (automated).** Verifies: PR-265. Check: `grep -in "BLOCKED" record.md` — cross-check every hit against the recorded decision. Pass: either zero dimensions are BLOCKED, or the decision is CONDITIONAL GO / NO-GO and each BLOCKED dimension appears as a dated condition or a cited no-go reason. Fail: block shipment — a GO recorded over a BLOCKED dimension is invalid (PR-265) and the decision is voided back to undecided. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-133 — Criteria-before-scores audit (manual).** Verifies: PR-263. Check: the reviewer compares the record's version history (or dated drafts) and confirms the criteria section's date precedes the earliest dimension score's date; any threshold edited after scoring must show the dimension re-scored with both versions retained. Pass: criteria demonstrably predate scores, or every post-hoc change has its re-score on file. Fail: block shipment; affected dimensions return to unscored and are re-scored against the standing criteria. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-134 — Payments live-fire evidence check (manual).** Verifies: PR-268. Check: for each payment method the record claims, inspect the attached live-environment evidence: one successful real charge, one failure-path record, and one completed refund, each dated and attributable to the production/live environment (provider dashboard export, transaction IDs), plus a screenshot or test record of the price/tax/receipt display in local currency and format. Pass: every claimed method has all three transaction records and the display check. Fail: the method is struck from the claimed set and the payments dimension is re-scored before any GO. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-135 — Claims-versus-record check (automated + manual).** Verifies: PR-280, PR-267. Check: `grep -rinE "now available|fully localized|now live|supports .*payment" launch-copy/` lists every public availability/localization/payment claim; the reviewer checks each against the record's decision status, the PR-267 tier, and the PR-268 live-tested method set. Pass: every claim matches the record exactly; the claimed localization level equals the signed-off tier. Fail: block publication of the offending copy until it is corrected to the record. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- One market, one record, one written decision — a verbal go is no go.
- Six dimensions, six verdicts, no average: a BLOCKED dimension blocks.
- Criteria before scores, or the scores are fiction.
- Payments are ready when a real charge and a real refund have happened, not when the logo is integrated.
- The local price is a decision with local evidence, never an exchange-rate conversion.

## Checklist

- [ ] Readiness record exists for this market with named owner and decider (PR-261).
- [ ] Criteria for all six dimensions were written before any scoring (PR-263, G-PR-133).
- [ ] All six dimensions scored separately with dated evidence; no averaged score anywhere (PR-264, PR-266, G-PR-131).
- [ ] Localization verdict copied from localization-workflow's tier and sign-off, not re-judged (PR-267).
- [ ] Every claimed payment method has a live charge, failure path, and refund on record (PR-268, G-PR-134).
- [ ] Legal dimension imported from privacy-laws / data-residency registers; entity, tax, and licence statuses recorded; no "required, not obtained" item scored above BLOCKED (PR-269).
- [ ] Local price set from in-market evidence and market unit economics, and handed to the fact sheet (PR-270, PR-275).
- [ ] Support named by person/team, language, hours in the market's timezone, and response target (PR-271).
- [ ] Named in-market reviewer walked the flows; every adaptation is done, dated, or waived in writing (PR-272).
- [ ] Demand section cites dated in-market evidence; market-size figures labeled context only (PR-273).
- [ ] Pilot defined with pre-registered success and kill thresholds and a review date (PR-274, PR-278).
- [ ] Exit plan written: user comms, money, surviving data obligations, exit owner (PR-277).
- [ ] Decision recorded as GO / CONDITIONAL GO / NO-GO, dated and signed; G-PR-132 blocker scan passes (PR-262, PR-265).
- [ ] Record carries a review/expiry date and is not reused as another market's evidence (PR-279).
- [ ] All public launch claims checked against the record before publication (PR-280, G-PR-135).

# personas-jtbd

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D1 Product & Requirements (PR)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Christensen Institute, "What is Jobs to Be Done Theory?" — https://www.christenseninstitute.org/video/what-is-jobs-to-be-done-theory/ ; Harvard Business School Online, "The Jobs to Be Done Framework" — https://online.hbs.edu/blog/post/jobs-to-be-done-examples
- **Depends on:** user-research
- **Feeds into:** user-stories, requirements-writing, roadmapping

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** research findings must be turned into a working set of personas; a trade-off discussion needs a named user and job to reason about; a story needs its role.
- **Do NOT use when:** no research findings exist yet (go to user-research first, or label the persona HYPOTHETICAL under PR-048). Never use a persona as public proof — testimonials and customer claims belong to real-content, sourced from real customers only.

## Rules

1. **PR-041 — Small set, one per job cluster.** The persona set holds 3–5 personas, one per distinct job cluster. Two personas with the same job are merged into one.
2. **PR-042 — JTBD format is exact.** Every persona's core need is written as: "When [situation], I want [motivation], so I can [expected outcome]." No other phrasing carries the job.
3. **PR-043 — Jobs name progress, not features.** The job statement names a circumstance and the progress sought. It never names a product feature, a screen, or a demographic as the job.
4. **PR-044 — Demographics earn their place.** A demographic attribute appears on a persona only where it changes the job or its constraints, and it cites the finding that shows the effect.
5. **PR-045 — Evidence-linked and versioned.** Each persona carries its evidence date and links to the finding IDs it was built from. Any change to the persona bumps its version.
6. **PR-046 — Forces before features.** For each persona's job, the forces of progress are analyzed — push of the current situation, pull of the new solution, anxiety about change, habit of the present — before any feature is proposed from that persona.
7. **PR-047 — Personas are cited in trade-offs.** A trade-off decision names the persona(s) and job(s) it serves. A decision naming neither is returned for rework.
8. **PR-048 — Real basis or labeled construct.** A persona built without research findings is labeled HYPOTHETICAL at the top of its card, holds no citation rights in requirements or copy, and is replaced or removed at the first real study.
9. **PR-049 — Representative tasks are observed tasks.** Each persona lists tasks drawn from research findings, phrased as the user phrases them — not tasks invented to match planned features.
10. **PR-050 — Retire dead personas.** A persona whose job cluster no longer appears in current research is archived with a date, not silently kept in the active set.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PR-021 — Stock-photo biography.** Banned: persona detail (name, age, hobbies, photo) with no research finding behind it. Defeats: DET-CON-019. Instead: build the persona from clustered findings and omit any biography no finding supports. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-022 — Feature stated as the job.** Banned: a JTBD statement whose "I want" is a product feature. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: "When the morning shift starts, I want to know which orders are late, so I can reassign drivers before customers call." Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-023 — Demographic-only persona.** Banned: segmenting personas by demographics alone ("Millennial moms", "Gen-Z users") with no distinct job behind the split. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: cluster by job; add demographics only where a finding shows they change the job (PR-044). Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-PR-024 — Persona quoted as proof.** Banned: using a persona as customer evidence in public copy, decks, or sales material. Defeats: DET-CON-010. Instead: testimonials come only from real customers with source records, handled by real-content; personas never appear in public copy. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-PR-021 — JTBD format lint.** Verifies: PR-042. Check: automated — run a regex over every JTBD statement confirming it matches the "When …, I want …, so I can …" pattern with all three parts non-empty. Pass: 100% match. Fail: block persona sign-off. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-022 — Evidence-link check.** Verifies: PR-045, PR-048. Check: automated — run a script confirming every persona carries at least one finding link that resolves in the research file, or carries the HYPOTHETICAL label. Pass: 100% of personas qualify one way or the other. Fail: block persona sign-off. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-023 — Job-distinctness review.** Verifies: PR-041. Check: manual — read all job statements side by side and confirm each names a different job. Pass: no two jobs are interchangeable. Fail: merge the duplicates and rework the set. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-024 — Forces completeness.** Verifies: PR-046. Check: manual — for each persona, confirm the forces section names push, pull, anxiety, and habit, each with a finding reference. Pass: all four present for every persona. Fail: warn, and block any feature proposal drawn from an incomplete persona. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- One persona per job cluster, three to five in total.
- When / I want / so I can — no other phrasing carries the job.
- Demographics appear only where they change the job.
- Forces before features.
- A persona is a reasoning tool, never public proof.

## Checklist

- [ ] The set holds 3–5 personas, one per distinct job (G-PR-023).
- [ ] Every JTBD statement passes the format lint (G-PR-021).
- [ ] Every persona carries finding links or the HYPOTHETICAL label (G-PR-022).
- [ ] No demographic appears without a finding showing it changes the job (PR-044).
- [ ] Push, pull, anxiety, and habit are recorded for every persona (G-PR-024).
- [ ] Recent trade-off decisions cite personas by name (PR-047).
- [ ] No persona text appears in any public-facing artifact (BAN-PR-024).

<!-- generated from skills/product-requirements/pricing-monetization/SKILL.md (bundle form) -->

# pricing-monetization

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D1 Product & Requirements (PR)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://stripe.com/resources/more/saas-pricing-and-packaging-strategy
- **Depends on:** competitive-analysis, unit-economics, fact-sheet
- **Feeds into:** fact-sheet, roadmapping

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** setting or changing prices, designing tiers or a free plan, launching a promotion, or auditing why the prices on different surfaces disagree.
- **Do NOT use when:** the question is whether the business model works at all (use unit-economics first), or the prices are one-off negotiated quotes with no published surfaces (record them in the fact sheet instead).

## Rules

1. **PR-201 — Value metric first.** Before any price is set, the value metric is chosen and written down: the quantity the customer pays more of as they receive more value (seats, projects, usage, revenue processed). Prices set before the value metric exists are provisional and marked as such.
2. **PR-202 — Model follows the metric.** The pricing model (per seat, tiered flat rate, usage-based, or hybrid) is chosen because it fits the value metric, and the fit is stated in one sentence in the pricing document.
3. **PR-203 — Tiers graduate naturally.** Tier boundaries sit where customers actually grow into the next level of value; a customer should hit a tier limit because they succeeded, not because an arbitrary feature was fenced off.
4. **PR-204 — One configuration, every surface.** Prices are implemented as billing-provider objects (products, prices, subscriptions). The pricing page, checkout, invoices, and emails render from that single configuration. There is no second price list anywhere.
5. **PR-205 — No hard-coded prices.** No price, plan name, or billing term is typed by hand into page copy, blog posts, emails, ads, or help articles. Surfaces that cannot render from the configuration link to the pricing page instead of restating the number.
6. **PR-206 — Fact sheet mirrors the configuration.** The fact sheet's price entries are copied from the billing configuration, and any conflict between the sheet and the configuration is resolved in favor of the configuration, with the sheet corrected the same day.
7. **PR-207 — Free tier has limits and a path.** A free tier states explicit limits (quantity, time, or capability) and a designed conversion path to paid. An unlimited free tier with no conversion design is a pricing defect.
8. **PR-208 — Promotions carry dates and terms.** Every discount or promotion shows its start, its end, and its terms wherever the promotional price appears. An undated promotional price is treated as an error and removed.
9. **PR-209 — Tier splits come from the value metric.** Which features sit in which tier is decided from the value metric and the upgrade path. Copying a competitor's three price points or feature fences without that derivation is not a pricing decision.
10. **PR-210 — No-provider fallback.** Where a project has no billing provider (quoted or brochure pricing), the fact sheet is the single price source of truth, every surface copies from it verbatim, and the consistency gate (G-PR-101) runs against the sheet instead of the provider.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PR-101 — Hand-typed price in copy.** Banned: typing a price into any page, post, email, or ad instead of rendering it from the billing configuration (or, under PR-210, copying it verbatim from the fact sheet). Defeats: DET-CON-016. Instead: render from the configuration, or link to the pricing page without restating the number (PR-205). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-102 — Undated promotion.** Banned: a discount, launch offer, or sale price shown without visible start/end dates and terms. Defeats: DET-CON-018. Instead: every promotion carries its dates and terms at the point of display (PR-208). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-103 — Invented price.** Banned: publishing a price, plan, or discount that exists in no billing configuration and no fact-sheet entry — created for one landing page or one ad. Defeats: DET-CON-016. Instead: create the price in the configuration first, then advertise it (PR-204). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-104 — Unlimited free tier.** Banned: a free tier with no stated limit on quantity, time, or capability and no conversion path. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: state the limits and design the upgrade path before the tier is announced (PR-207). Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-PR-101 — Price-consistency scan.** Verifies: PR-204, PR-205, PR-206. Check (automated): extract every price and plan mention across the site (for example `grep -rEo '\$[0-9]+(\.[0-9]{2})?/(mo|month|yr|year)' site/ | sort | uniq -c`) and diff the set against the billing provider's active price list (or the fact sheet under PR-210). Pass: every published price matches exactly one configured price, and every plan name matches. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-102 — Test-mode checkout and upgrade run.** Verifies: PR-203, PR-204. Check (automated where the provider supports test mode): complete a test purchase of each tier, then a mid-cycle upgrade; compare charged totals, proration, and resulting entitlements against the pricing page. Pass: totals and entitlements match the published page for every tier. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-103 — Promotion date sweep.** Verifies: PR-208. Check (automated): `grep -rniE "off|discount|sale|offer" site/` lists every promotional surface; each must contain a date or date range on the same page. Pass: zero undated promotions. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-104 — Value-metric review.** Verifies: PR-201, PR-209. Check (manual): the pricing document states the value metric, the model-fit sentence, and the derivation of each tier split. Pass: all three present and the tier splits cite the value metric rather than a competitor. Fail: warn; pricing changes pause until the document is completed. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Value metric first; model second; numbers last.
- One configuration renders every price surface.
- A price typed by hand is a future mismatch.
- Every promotion carries its dates, or it comes down.
- Free tiers have limits and a path, or they are defects.

## Checklist

- [ ] Value metric written down before prices were set (PR-201).
- [ ] Model-fit sentence recorded in the pricing document (PR-202, G-PR-104).
- [ ] All prices exist as billing-provider objects; no second price list (PR-204).
- [ ] No hand-typed prices anywhere in copy, email, or ads (PR-205, G-PR-101).
- [ ] Fact sheet prices match the configuration (PR-206).
- [ ] Free tier limits and conversion path stated (PR-207).
- [ ] Every live promotion shows dates and terms (PR-208, G-PR-103).
- [ ] Test checkout and upgrade totals verified against the pricing page (G-PR-102).

<!-- generated from skills/product-requirements/product-metrics/SKILL.md (bundle form) -->

# product-metrics

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D1 Product & Requirements (PR)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://info.amplitude.com/rs/138-CDN-550/images/ai-product-metrics-worksheet-bundle.pdf
- **Depends on:** discovery, fact-sheet
- **Feeds into:** roadmapping, unit-economics, scope-control

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** choosing the metrics a product or release will be judged by; writing or changing a metric definition; setting up a dashboard; preparing any number for publication in copy, decks, or the fact sheet.
- **Do NOT use when:** the numbers are financial per-customer economics (use unit-economics), or the task is instrumenting events in code (this skill defines what must exist; implementation follows the definition).

## Rules

1. **PR-181 — One North Star, value first.** The product has exactly one North Star metric, and it captures the value customers get, stated in plain words. The North Star leads revenue; it is never revenue itself.
2. **PR-182 — Three to five input metrics.** The North Star is decomposed into 3–5 input metrics spanning breadth, depth, frequency, and efficiency — levers a team can move weekly, not outcomes it can only watch.
3. **PR-183 — Exact written definitions.** Every metric has a definition in the metric dictionary stating the event, the time window, the segment, and the exclusions. A metric that cannot be defined this precisely is not yet a metric.
4. **PR-184 — Owner and source for every metric.** Each dictionary entry names an owning team and the data source (system and query or report) the number comes from.
5. **PR-185 — Definitions are versioned.** A definition change is a changelog entry with date, old definition, new definition, and reason. Numbers computed under different definitions are never trended together without a visible break marker.
6. **PR-186 — Nothing publishes without a definition and a source.** No number appears in copy, decks, investor material, or the fact sheet unless it resolves to a dictionary definition and a queryable source.
7. **PR-187 — Guardrails are named.** The framework names the guardrail metrics that must not degrade while the North Star grows (for example: error rate, support tickets per active account, churn).
8. **PR-188 — Vanity metrics are not success.** Registrations, raw pageviews, and total accounts may be reported as context but never serve as the success measure for a product, release, or experiment. The North Star must rise only when customers succeed.
9. **PR-189 — Inputs are re-validated against outcomes.** At each metric review, input metrics are checked against the North Star: an input that no longer predicts it is replaced, and the replacement is recorded in the changelog.
10. **PR-190 — Every input has a team that can move it.** An input metric no named team can influence is decoration; it is removed from the framework or reassigned until an owner with real leverage exists.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PR-091 — Publishing an undefined number.** Banned: putting a metric in copy, a deck, or the fact sheet that has no dictionary definition or no queryable source behind it. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: define the metric, compute it from its source, then publish the figure with its definition available (PR-183, PR-186). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-092 — Silent redefinition.** Banned: changing what a metric counts (window, exclusions, event) without a changelog entry, so the trend line silently mixes two different measures. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: version the definition under PR-185 and mark the break. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-093 — Dashboard metric with no dictionary entry.** Banned: a chart or KPI tile on any dashboard whose metric does not exist in the dictionary with definition, owner, and source. Defeats: DET-CON-014. Instead: add the dictionary entry first, or remove the tile (PR-184). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-094 — Vanity count as success proof.** Banned: presenting a vanity count (total signups, total downloads, raw pageviews) as evidence that customers succeed or that the product is growing in value. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: report the North Star and its inputs; vanity counts appear only as labeled context (PR-188). Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-PR-091 — Dictionary completeness scan.** Verifies: PR-183, PR-184, PR-186. Check (automated): list every metric name displayed on any dashboard or report; for each, `grep -i "<metric name>" metric-dictionary.md` must find an entry containing definition, owner, and source fields. Pass: zero displayed metrics missing a complete entry. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-092 — Instrumentation name check.** Verifies: PR-183. Check (automated): for each dictionary definition, extract the named event and run `grep -rn "<event_name>" analytics/ src/` (or query the analytics tool's event list) to confirm the event exists under exactly that name. Pass: every definition's event found under the same name. Fail: block shipment — a definition naming a non-existent event measures nothing. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-093 — Definition changelog audit.** Verifies: PR-185. Check (automated): `grep -c "definition changed" metric-dictionary.md` is compared against the count of definition edits in the file's version history for the period; any edit without a matching changelog entry is flagged. Pass: zero unlogged definition edits. Fail: warn; the changelog is completed before the next report ships. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-094 — North Star sanity review.** Verifies: PR-181, PR-188. Check (manual): read the North Star statement and answer two questions in writing — does it rise only when customers succeed, and does it lead rather than equal revenue? Pass: both answers are yes with a one-line justification each. Fail: block shipment of the framework until the North Star is rewritten. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- One North Star: customer value, leading revenue, never revenue itself.
- No definition, no dashboard; no source, no publication.
- Definition changes are changelog entries, never edits in the night.
- Vanity counts are context, not success.
- An input nobody can move is decoration.

## Checklist

- [ ] Exactly one North Star, stated as customer value (PR-181, G-PR-094).
- [ ] 3–5 input metrics across breadth, depth, frequency, efficiency (PR-182).
- [ ] Every metric defined exactly: event, window, segment, exclusions (PR-183).
- [ ] Every dictionary entry names owner and data source (PR-184, G-PR-091).
- [ ] Instrumentation events exist under the dictionary's names (G-PR-092).
- [ ] All definition changes since last review are in the changelog (PR-185, G-PR-093).
- [ ] Guardrail metrics named (PR-187).
- [ ] No number queued for publication lacks a definition and a source (PR-186).

# requirements-writing

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D1 Product & Requirements (PR)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018, IEEE Standards Association — https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/29148/6937/ ; 29148 tutorial and characteristic list — https://www.xopsschool.com/mod/page/view.php?id=3365
- **Depends on:** discovery, user-research, personas-jtbd
- **Feeds into:** user-stories, acceptance-criteria, scope-control

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** stakeholder needs must become a specification a builder can implement and a tester can verify; a requirement set is being drafted, reviewed, or changed.
- **Do NOT use when:** the need itself is still unexplored (discovery and user-research come first) or the work item is an iteration-sized story (user-stories). Do not write requirements to document a design that was already chosen — that reverses the trace.

## Rules

1. **PR-061 — One obligation per requirement.** Each requirement carries exactly one "shall". A requirement containing two obligations is split into two requirements before review.
2. **PR-062 — Mandatory attributes.** Every requirement carries a unique ID, source (stakeholder need or finding), priority, rationale, and verification method. A requirement missing any attribute is incomplete and cannot be baselined.
3. **PR-063 — Vague terms need numbers.** The terms fast, user-friendly, robust, seamless, flexible, and their synonyms are banned unless the same sentence states the measurable criterion the term stands for.
4. **PR-064 — Need, not design.** Requirements state the need. An implementation choice appears only as a labeled design constraint backed by a real external constraint, which is named.
5. **PR-065 — Conflicts resolved on record.** Conflicting requirements are resolved explicitly and the resolution is recorded with its decider. Wording is never averaged to hide a conflict.
6. **PR-066 — Bidirectional traceability.** Every requirement traces back to a stakeholder need and forward to at least one design element and one acceptance test. An orphan in either direction is a defect.
7. **PR-067 — Changes are versioned.** A requirement change goes through review and appears in the version history with date and decider. A silently edited requirement is treated as new and unvalidated.
8. **PR-068 — Set-level completeness.** Before handoff, the set is checked as a whole: every stakeholder need is covered by at least one requirement, and no two requirements contradict each other.
9. **PR-069 — Verifiable by construction.** Each requirement names its verification method (test, demonstration, inspection, or analysis) at the time it is written. A requirement with no method is rewritten until it has one.
10. **PR-070 — Negative requirements are explicit.** What the system must not do — data it must not retain, behaviors it must forbid — is written as requirements, not left implied by the positive ones.
11. **PR-071 — One priority per requirement.** Each requirement carries exactly one priority from the project's scheme. A requirement marked with two priorities is resolved before handoff.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PR-031 — The compound requirement.** Banned: one requirement ID carrying two or more obligations. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: three requirements, one obligation each, each with its own verification method. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-032 — The adjective requirement.** Banned: a requirement whose only success test is a vague adjective. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: "The dashboard shall render first contentful paint within 2.0 seconds on the reference device against the reference dataset." Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-033 — The silent edit.** Banned: changing a requirement's text without a version-history entry. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: edit, add a history entry (date, decider, reason), and notify the owners of linked artifacts. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-034 — Solution smuggled in as a need.** Banned: prescribing an implementation as a requirement with no external constraint behind it. Defeats: DET-CON-014. Instead: state the need ("The configurator flow shall update without full page reloads") or label the item a design constraint and name its external source. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-PR-031 — Requirement lint.** Verifies: PR-061, PR-062, PR-063. Check: automated — run a script over the requirements file confirming (a) ID, source, priority, rationale, and verification method are present and non-empty for 100% of requirements, (b) each requirement contains exactly one "shall", and (c) every banned vague term is flagged unless its sentence contains a number or unit. Pass: zero violations. Fail: block handoff. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-032 — Traceability coverage.** Verifies: PR-066. Check: automated — generate the coverage report: every Must-priority requirement has at least one linked source need and at least one linked acceptance criterion or test. Pass: 100% coverage. Fail: block handoff to build. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-033 — Conflict and set review.** Verifies: PR-065, PR-068. Check: manual — review the set against the stakeholder need list: confirm full coverage and read every recorded conflict for its resolution and decider. Pass: no uncovered need, no unresolved conflict. Fail: block handoff. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-034 — Change-history audit.** Verifies: PR-067. Check: automated — diff the current requirements against the last baselined version; every changed ID must appear in the version history. Pass: 100% of changes logged. Fail: warn, and unlogged changes revert to unvalidated status until reviewed. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- One shall, one obligation, one requirement.
- No number, no adjective.
- Need first; design only as a labeled constraint.
- Every requirement traces backward and forward.
- A silent edit makes a new requirement.

## Checklist

- [ ] Requirement lint passes with zero violations (G-PR-031).
- [ ] Every requirement carries ID, source, priority, rationale, and verification method (PR-062).
- [ ] Traceability coverage is 100% for Must requirements (G-PR-032).
- [ ] All conflicts carry a recorded resolution and decider (PR-065).
- [ ] Negative requirements are written, not implied (PR-070).
- [ ] Every change since baseline appears in the version history (G-PR-034).
- [ ] The set covers every stakeholder need (PR-068).
