<!-- generated from skills/product-requirements/roadmapping/SKILL.md (bundle form) -->

# roadmapping

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D1 Product & Requirements (PR)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://www.prodpad.com/glossary/now-next-later-roadmap/
- **Depends on:** discovery, scope-control, acceptance-criteria
- **Feeds into:** user-stories, requirements-writing

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** sequencing product work across quarters; publishing or updating an internal or public roadmap; moving an initiative between horizons; answering "when will X ship?" with something honest.
- **Do NOT use when:** the decision is what fits inside one fixed release (use scope-control), or the item has no discovery behind it yet and belongs in the opportunity tree, not on any roadmap horizon (use discovery).

## Rules

1. **PR-241 — Three confidence horizons.** The roadmap uses Now / Next / Later. Now = validated initiatives in active build. Next = problems under active discovery. Later = strategic bets not yet shaped. An item's horizon states the team's confidence, not a delivery slot.
2. **PR-242 — Outcomes, not features.** Every item is framed as an outcome or problem linked to a named objective ("cut time-to-first-report for new accounts"), not as a feature name ("reporting module v2").
3. **PR-243 — No dates outside Now.** Next and Later items carry no calendar dates and no quarter labels presented as commitments. A date on a Later item is a promise the team has not validated.
4. **PR-244 — Now requires discovery.** An item enters Now only after discovery (a target opportunity plus assumption tests, per discovery) and with acceptance criteria attached or explicitly scheduled before build starts.
5. **PR-245 — Entry through the tree and a class.** Items reach the roadmap through the opportunity tree and carry a MoSCoW class from scope-control. Stakeholder volume and seniority are not entry criteria.
6. **PR-246 — Placement by evidence.** Horizon placement is set by the strength of discovery evidence and stated confidence, and the placement rationale is written on the item. Confidence, not optimism, moves items forward.
7. **PR-247 — External is less specific.** The public roadmap is deliberately less specific than the internal one: outcomes and horizons only, no dates, no unvalidated capabilities. Anything public is a product promise.
8. **PR-248 — Every change is recorded.** Each roadmap change records what moved, why, and what it displaced. Silent re-sequencing — in either the internal or the public view — is a defect.
9. **PR-249 — Later items expire.** Later items carry a review interval. An item not reviewed within that interval is flagged for re-triage: re-validate, demote to the opportunity tree, or remove it.
10. **PR-250 — Two views, one truth.** The internal and external roadmaps are generated from the same item list. The external view may say less, but it may never say something different.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PR-121 — Date on an unvalidated item.** Banned: placing a calendar date or committed quarter on a Next or Later item. Defeats: DET-CON-018. Instead: keep the item in its horizon with its confidence stated (PR-243). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-122 — Public promise ahead of internal validation.** Banned: listing a capability on the public roadmap that the internal roadmap has not validated through discovery. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: the public entry waits for internal validation, or is framed as an outcome under exploration (PR-247). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-123 — "Coming soon" with no horizon.** Banned: a public "coming soon" feature announcement that names no horizon, no discovery status, and no review date. Defeats: DET-CON-004. Instead: publish through the roadmap's horizons, or do not announce (PR-247). Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-PR-124 — Silent re-sequencing.** Banned: moving, swapping, or dropping roadmap items without a change record stating what moved, why, and what it displaced. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: record the change under PR-248 in both views. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-PR-121 — Roadmap field check.** Verifies: PR-241, PR-242, PR-244. Check (automated): every item in the roadmap file carries the fields outcome, objective, horizon, and — for Now items — a discovery link; a field-presence scan returns zero incomplete items. Pass: zero incomplete items. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-122 — Date scan.** Verifies: PR-243. Check (automated): `grep -nE "20[0-9]{2}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])|Q[1-4] 20[0-9]{2}" roadmap.md` restricted to the Next and Later sections must return no date or quarter commitments. Pass: zero hits in those sections. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-123 — Staleness check.** Verifies: PR-249. Check (automated): each Later item's last-reviewed date is compared against the stated review interval; items past the interval are listed. Pass: zero unreviewed Later items, or each is flagged in the document as awaiting re-triage. Fail: warn. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-124 — Two-view consistency diff.** Verifies: PR-247, PR-250. Check (manual): place the public roadmap beside the internal one; every public item must exist internally at the same or greater specificity, and no public item may assert a capability, date, or commitment absent internally. Pass: zero public assertions without an internal source. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Horizons state confidence, not delivery slots.
- No dates outside Now — a dated Later item is an unvalidated promise.
- The public roadmap may say less, never something different.
- Items enter through discovery and a MoSCoW class, not volume.
- Every move records what it displaced.

## Checklist

- [ ] All items sit in Now, Next, or Later with confidence stated (PR-241).
- [ ] Every item framed as an outcome linked to an objective (PR-242, G-PR-121).
- [ ] No dates or committed quarters on Next/Later items (PR-243, G-PR-122).
- [ ] Every Now item has discovery evidence and acceptance criteria attached or scheduled (PR-244).
- [ ] Entry path recorded: opportunity tree plus MoSCoW class (PR-245).
- [ ] Public view checked against internal view — less specific, never different (PR-247, PR-250, G-PR-124).
- [ ] All changes since last publication logged with reason and displacement (PR-248).
- [ ] No Later item past its review interval unflagged (PR-249, G-PR-123).

<!-- generated from skills/product-requirements/scope-control/SKILL.md (bundle form) -->

# scope-control

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D1 Product & Requirements (PR)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://projeric.com/blogs/scope-management/moscow-prioritization ; https://resources.rework.com/libraries/project-management/moscow-prioritization
- **Depends on:** requirements-writing
- **Feeds into:** roadmapping, user-stories

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a release or iteration has a fixed timeframe and more candidate work than capacity; a scope document is being written, re-triaged, or changed mid-flight; public copy is about to describe what the release includes.
- **Do NOT use when:** there is no requirements list yet (use requirements-writing first), or the question is long-term sequencing rather than this release's boundary (use roadmapping).

## Rules

1. **PR-141 — Four classes, always.** Every scope document classifies every candidate item as Must, Should, Could, or Won't have (this time), per DSDM/MoSCoW. An item with no class is not in scope and not out of scope — it is undecided, and undecided items never reach build or copy.
2. **PR-142 — Non-empty Won't-have list.** The scope document contains a Won't have (this time) section with at least one named item. A boundary that excludes nothing bounds nothing.
3. **PR-143 — Every Must traces to an objective.** Each Must have carries a link to the stated project objective it serves. A Must with no objective is demoted to Should pending review.
4. **PR-144 — Must effort capped at ~60%.** Must haves total no more than about 60% of the timeframe's estimated effort, measured by effort, not by item count, so Should and Could items act as contingency.
5. **PR-145 — Over-cap Musts force re-triage.** If estimated Must effort exceeds ~60% of capacity, re-triage happens before build starts. Proceeding anyway is a defect, not enthusiasm — unless the release records an explicit override, mirroring PR-224 in unit-economics: the override note states that the cap is exceeded, the reason, and the contingency risk accepted. An unrecorded over-cap is still a defect.
6. **PR-146 — Fixed de-scope order.** When the timeframe is threatened, items are cut in the agreed order: Could first, then Should. Musts and the date hold unless the release is re-baselined under PR-147.
7. **PR-147 — Changes displace or re-baseline.** A scope change enters only by displacing equal estimated effort from a lower class, or by a recorded re-baseline of the release (new date or new capacity) approved by the decider named in the document.
8. **PR-148 — Every change is logged.** Each scope change records the item, the decider, the date, and what it displaced. An unlogged change is treated as never approved.
9. **PR-149 — Public copy mirrors Must and Should only.** Marketing pages, changelogs, and sales material may describe Must and Should items as included. Could items are never presented as included, and Won't-have items are never presented at all.
10. **PR-150 — Owner and review date.** The scope document names one owner and a review date. A scope document past its review date cannot authorize new commitments until re-reviewed.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PR-071 — Unscoped feature in public copy.** Banned: describing a feature in marketing copy, a changelog, or a sales deck when the scope document classes it Could or Won't have (this time). Defeats: DET-CON-004. Instead: copy is written from the Must and Should classes only (PR-149). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-072 — Dated promise for unvalidated scope.** Banned: attaching a launch date or "coming soon" announcement to any item that is not a Must have with acceptance criteria attached. Defeats: DET-CON-018. Instead: announce only Must items, and only with the release's own date. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-073 — Silent scope absorption.** Banned: adding an item to the build without a change-log entry naming the decider and the displaced item. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: log the change under PR-148 before build starts. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-074 — Promising a scope item as an operational commitment.** Banned: copy that commits the business to an ongoing service (support hours, uptime, response times) that no scope item or policy funds. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: the promise is scoped and funded first, or the copy is cut. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-PR-071 — Won't-have presence check.** Verifies: PR-141, PR-142. Check (automated): `sed -n "/won't have/I,/^## /p" scope.md | grep -q "^- "` — the Won't have section must contain at least one list item. Pass: command exits 0. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-072 — Must effort-share computation.** Verifies: PR-144, PR-145. Check (automated): export the requirements table to CSV (columns: item,class,effort) and run `awk -F, '$2=="Must"{m+=$3} {t+=$3} END {print m/t}' requirements.csv`. Pass: output ≤ 0.60. Fail: block shipment until re-triage is recorded. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-073 — Must-to-objective trace check.** Verifies: PR-143. Check (automated): every row classed Must in the requirements table has a non-empty objective column; a script or spreadsheet filter for `class=Must AND objective=""` must return zero rows. Pass: zero rows. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-074 — Change-log audit.** Verifies: PR-147, PR-148. Check (manual): diff the current scope document against its previous version; every added or reclassed item must have a matching change-log entry with decider, date, and displaced item. Pass: zero unexplained diffs. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-075 — Copy-to-scope sweep.** Verifies: PR-149. Check (manual): list every feature named in the release's public copy; each must appear in the scope document as Must or Should. Pass: zero features sourced from Could or Won't have. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Four classes or it is not a scope document.
- A boundary that excludes nothing bounds nothing.
- Musts ≤ ~60% of effort — the rest is contingency.
- Changes displace, or the release is re-baselined. Never both silently.
- Public copy mirrors Must and Should only.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every candidate item carries a MoSCoW class (PR-141).
- [ ] Won't have (this time) section exists and is non-empty (PR-142, G-PR-071).
- [ ] Every Must links to a stated objective (PR-143, G-PR-073).
- [ ] Must effort share computed and ≤ ~60% (PR-144, G-PR-072).
- [ ] De-scope order (Could, then Should) written in the document (PR-146).
- [ ] Every change since the last version is logged with decider, date, and displacement (PR-148, G-PR-074).
- [ ] Public copy checked against Must/Should classes only (PR-149, G-PR-075).
- [ ] Owner and review date present and current (PR-150).

<!-- generated from skills/product-requirements/unit-economics/SKILL.md (bundle form) -->

# unit-economics

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D1 Product & Requirements (PR)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://www.forentrepreneurs.com/ltv-cac/ ; https://www.construx.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/CxWhitePaper_ConeOfUncertainty.pdf
- **Depends on:** product-metrics, pricing-monetization
- **Feeds into:** scope-control, roadmapping

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** judging whether an acquisition motion or business model can work; computing or publishing CAC, LTV, their ratio, or payback; producing a cost or effort estimate for a project, feature, or plan.
- **Do NOT use when:** the acquisition motion does not exist yet and the honest output is "directional only" (say so and stop), or the numbers are published marketing metrics rather than economics (use product-metrics).

## Rules

1. **PR-221 — CAC is fully loaded.** CAC = (all sales + marketing cost for the period) ÷ (new customers acquired in the same period). "All" includes salaries, commissions, tools, agencies, and content production — never media spend alone.
2. **PR-222 — LTV is margin-based.** LTV = average revenue per account × gross margin ÷ churn rate, with revenue, margin, and churn stated for the same cohort and period. Revenue-based LTV is never reported as LTV.
3. **PR-223 — Payback uses gross profit.** CAC payback (months) = CAC ÷ monthly gross profit per customer. Ratio and payback are always reported together; either one alone hides the cash problem or the value problem.
4. **PR-224 — Heuristics are heuristics.** LTV:CAC above 3 and payback under 12 months are viability heuristics (Skok), recorded as defaults with an explicit override note when a project departs from them — never applied as universal pass/fail laws to non-SaaS models.
5. **PR-225 — No ratio before a repeatable motion.** LTV:CAC is not computed as a decision number until a repeatable acquisition motion exists. Figures computed earlier are labeled "directional" wherever they appear and cannot anchor commitments.
6. **PR-226 — Estimates are ranges with a method.** Every estimate states a range, the named assumptions, and the method used (analogy, decomposition, or parametric). A single-point estimate with none of these fails review.
7. **PR-227 — Estimate, target, commitment are separate.** The estimate (what the work is expected to take), the target (what the business wants), and the commitment (what was promised externally) are three distinct numbers, recorded separately and never silently merged.
8. **PR-228 — Estimate vs. actual is logged.** Every completed item records its estimate and its actual. A team with no such history states in writing that its estimates are uncalibrated guesses.
9. **PR-229 — Cohort before aggregate.** Economics are computed per cohort or segment first. A blended figure that hides a losing segment is a reporting defect, and the losing segment is reported, not averaged away.
10. **PR-230 — Cone position is stated.** Early estimates name their position on McConnell's Cone of Uncertainty (an initial-concept estimate can run 0.25x–4x the actual) and narrow only as named decisions and decomposition reduce the uncertainty.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PR-111 — Media-only CAC.** Banned: computing CAC from advertising spend alone, excluding salaries, commissions, tools, and agency cost. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: fully load the numerator under PR-221. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-112 — Revenue LTV labeled as LTV.** Banned: dividing revenue per account by churn and presenting the result as LTV without applying gross margin. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: apply margin under PR-222 and show both inputs. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-113 — Single-point estimate.** Banned: quoting one number ("$80k, three months") with no range, no assumptions, and no method. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: estimate under PR-226 and PR-230. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-114 — Blended ratio hiding a losing segment.** Banned: publishing one blended LTV:CAC while a named segment's ratio is below 1 and undisclosed. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: report per-cohort figures first (PR-229). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-PR-111 — Formula audit.** Verifies: PR-221, PR-222, PR-223. Check (automated): recompute CAC, LTV, ratio, and payback from the raw inputs with a script or spreadsheet and diff against the reported figures (tolerance: rounding only). Pass: all four recomputed values match the report. Fail: block shipment of the report. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-112 — Estimate-record check.** Verifies: PR-226, PR-227, PR-230. Check (automated): every estimate record contains the fields range-low, range-high, method, assumptions, cone-position, and separate estimate/target/commitment values; a field-presence scan over the estimates file returns zero incomplete records. Pass: zero incomplete records. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-113 — Cohort disclosure check.** Verifies: PR-229. Check (automated): any document reporting a blended LTV, CAC, or ratio must also contain a per-cohort table; `grep -ci "cohort" report.md` ≥ 1 wherever a blended figure appears, and each cohort row shows its own ratio. Pass: blended figures never appear without the cohort table. Fail: warn; the table is added before the figures are used in a decision. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-114 — Calibration log review.** Verifies: PR-228. Check (manual): open the estimate-vs-actual log; the last five completed items have both numbers recorded, or the document states that the team is uncalibrated. Pass: log current or the uncalibrated statement present. Fail: warn. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- CAC is fully loaded or it is fiction.
- LTV is margin-based, or it is revenue wearing a costume.
- Ratio and payback travel together.
- Estimates are ranges with assumptions; single points are promises.
- Cohort before aggregate — blends hide losers.

## Checklist

- [ ] CAC numerator includes salaries, commissions, tools, agencies, content (PR-221, G-PR-111).
- [ ] LTV computed from margin, with revenue, margin, and churn stated (PR-222).
- [ ] Payback reported alongside the ratio (PR-223).
- [ ] Heuristic departures recorded as overrides, not hidden (PR-224).
- [ ] Pre-motion figures labeled "directional" (PR-225).
- [ ] Every estimate carries range, method, assumptions, cone position (PR-226, PR-230, G-PR-112).
- [ ] Estimate, target, and commitment recorded as three numbers (PR-227).
- [ ] Estimate-vs-actual log current for the last completed items (PR-228, G-PR-114).
- [ ] Cohort table present wherever a blended figure appears (PR-229, G-PR-113).

# user-research

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D1 Product & Requirements (PR)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Nielsen Norman Group, "Personas Make Users Memorable for Product Team Members" — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/persona/ ; Torres, Opportunity Solution Tree — https://www.chameleon.io/blog/opportunity-solution-tree
- **Depends on:** discovery
- **Feeds into:** personas-jtbd, requirements-writing

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** evidence about users must be gathered, recorded, or cited — before personas are built, before a segment claim is made, before a requirement claims user backing.
- **Do NOT use when:** the question is what to build next (that is discovery working from this evidence) or how a claim may be published (that is fact-sheet and real-content). Do not run "research" whose only source is the team's own opinion.

## Rules

1. **PR-021 — Findings before interpretations.** The research file writes findings (what was observed) separately from interpretations (what the team concludes). The two are never merged into a single statement.
2. **PR-022 — Every study is fully attributed.** Each study entry records method, participant count, participant source, and dates. An entry missing any of the four is incomplete and cannot be cited.
3. **PR-023 — Real segment only.** Participants come from the actual target segment. Team members, friends, and other builders never count as user evidence.
4. **PR-024 — No claim without a citation.** No persona, segment claim, or "users want X" statement exists without a cited finding ID behind it.
5. **PR-025 — Sample limits are stated.** Every study states who was not reached and what the sample cannot support; the limit is part of the finding.
6. **PR-026 — Context travels with quotes.** Every quote or observation keeps its context (task, moment, segment). A decontextualized quote is not evidence.
7. **PR-027 — Staleness is enforced.** Research past its stated refresh date is marked STALE in the file and cannot justify new commitments until refreshed.
8. **PR-028 — Triangulation for load-bearing claims.** A claim that a persona or requirement depends on is corroborated by a second source type (survey, support tickets, or analytics alongside interviews).
9. **PR-029 — Raw records are kept.** The notes or recordings the method allows are stored with the study, so any finding can be re-checked against its source.
10. **PR-030 — Supplied-material honesty.** When research is built from user-supplied material rather than studies the team ran, the file says so and names the material; anything inferred from it is labeled an inference.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PR-011 — The uncited "users want".** Banned: any "users want / need / prefer X" statement in a research artifact with no finding ID behind it. Defeats: DET-CON-014. Instead: cite the finding ("F-07: 6 of 9 dispatchers exported reports to phone spreadsheets during the March study") or delete the claim. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-012 — Invented participants.** Banned: participant counts, quotes, or studies that were never run. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: record what actually happened ("3 support tickets, March export, supplied by the user"). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-013 — Colleague-as-user.** Banned: counting team members, friends, or role-play sessions as research participants. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: recruit from the target segment, or label the session an internal review, not research. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-014 — Stale research presented as current.** Banned: citing research past its refresh date as justification for a new commitment without showing the date and the STALE mark. Defeats: DET-CON-018. Instead: show the date and the STALE mark, or refresh the study first. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-PR-011 — Study-field completeness.** Verifies: PR-022. Check: automated — run a template check over the research file confirming every study entry has non-empty method, participant count/source, and date fields. Pass: 100% of entries complete. Fail: block citation of the incomplete studies. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-012 — Persona traceability.** Verifies: PR-024. Check: automated — run a script confirming every persona in the persona file cites at least one finding ID that exists in the research file. Pass: 100% of citations resolve. Fail: block persona sign-off. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-013 — Claim citation audit.** Verifies: PR-024, PR-028. Check: manual — sample 5 load-bearing claims in downstream artifacts; each must resolve to a finding, and load-bearing claims to two source types. Pass: 5 of 5 resolve. Fail: warn; a repeat failure blocks handoff. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-014 — Staleness sweep.** Verifies: PR-027. Check: automated — compare each study's refresh date against today's date and flag overdue studies STALE in the file. Pass: no overdue study remains unmarked. Fail: warn, and mark before any further citation. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Findings and interpretations live in separate sections.
- Method, count, source, date — or it did not happen.
- No claim without a finding ID.
- Who was not reached is part of the finding.
- Stale research is marked, never silently reused.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every study entry has method, participant count/source, and dates (G-PR-011).
- [ ] Findings and interpretations are in separate sections (PR-021).
- [ ] No participant comes from outside the target segment (PR-023).
- [ ] Every downstream claim sampled resolves to a finding ID (G-PR-013).
- [ ] Each study states who was not reached (PR-025).
- [ ] No overdue study is unmarked STALE (G-PR-014).
- [ ] Supplied material is named as supplied, with inferences labeled (PR-030).

<!-- generated from skills/product-requirements/user-stories/SKILL.md (bundle form) -->

# user-stories

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D1 Product & Requirements (PR)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Mike Cohn / Mountain Goat Software, "What Makes a Good User Story?" (INVEST) — https://www.mountaingoatsoftware.com/agile/user-stories/good-user-stories
- **Depends on:** personas-jtbd, requirements-writing
- **Feeds into:** acceptance-criteria, scope-control

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** validated needs and requirements must become iteration-sized work items a team can build and confirm; a backlog is being refined.
- **Do NOT use when:** the work has no user-visible benefit (label it a task under PR-084), or the need behind the item has not been validated (return to discovery). Do not use story format to give technical work borrowed legitimacy.

## Rules

1. **PR-081 — Template is mandatory.** Every story reads: "As a [role], I want [capability], so that [benefit]." All three parts are present and non-empty.
2. **PR-082 — The role is a named persona.** The role names a persona or segment from the persona set. Bare "user" is allowed only when the capability serves every segment identically, and the story states that reason on its face.
3. **PR-083 — The benefit clause is real.** The "so that" states an outcome the role values. A clause that restates the capability ("so that I can use the feature") fails.
4. **PR-084 — Tasks are labeled tasks.** Work with no user-visible benefit — endpoints, migrations, refactors — is labeled a task and planned as one. It never wears story format.
5. **PR-085 — One iteration maximum.** A story too big to finish in one iteration is split before estimation, along workflow steps or business rules — never along technical layers.
6. **PR-086 — No story without criteria.** A story enters build only with at least one linked acceptance criterion (see acceptance-criteria).
7. **PR-087 — The conversation is recorded.** Decisions from the story conversation (card–conversation–confirmation) are written on the story before build. An unrecorded agreement does not exist.
8. **PR-088 — Splits keep value whole.** Each story produced by a split still delivers a complete, usable slice of value to its role. A split producing a fragment nobody can use is re-split.
9. **PR-089 — Stories trace upward.** Each story links to its parent opportunity ID or requirement ID, which must resolve.
10. **PR-090 — INVEST is a diagnostic, not a score.** Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, and Testable are checked at refinement; a failing letter triggers a fix or a recorded exception — never a points chase.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PR-041 — The bare-user story.** Banned: "As a user…" where segments differ in need, permission, or outcome. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: "As a dispatch lead, I want to export the filtered order list, so that I can send month-end totals to finance." Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-042 — The disguised task.** Banned: technical work dressed as a story to borrow its legitimacy. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: label it a task, link it to the story it enables, and plan it as engineering work. Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-PR-043 — The benefit-less story.** Banned: a story with no "so that" clause, or a clause that restates the capability. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: "As a dispatch lead, I want late orders flagged on one screen, so that I can reassign drivers before customers call." Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PR-044 — The epic in story's clothing.** Banned: estimating or scheduling, as a single story, work that cannot finish in one iteration. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: split along the workflow (view late orders → export totals → schedule recurring sends) and estimate the pieces. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-PR-041 — Story template lint.** Verifies: PR-081, PR-082, PR-083. Check: automated — run a regex over every story confirming the "As a [role], I want [capability], so that [benefit]" shape, and that the role matches a persona name or carries the all-segments note. Pass: 100% of stories conform. Fail: block refinement sign-off. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-042 — Criteria linkage.** Verifies: PR-086. Check: automated — run a tracker query confirming no story in "in build" status has zero linked acceptance criteria. Pass: zero violations. Fail: block the status change until criteria are attached. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-043 — Split review.** Verifies: PR-085, PR-088. Check: manual — every story estimated above the team's one-iteration threshold shows its split, and each child story delivers usable value on its own. The review also judges each story's benefit clause: a benefit that merely repeats the capability text (a semantic judgment no lint can make) is sent back for rewriting. Pass: all oversized stories are split into whole-value pieces and no benefit clause repeats its capability. Fail: block estimation. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PR-044 — Traceability spot check.** Verifies: PR-089. Check: automated — run a script confirming every story carries an opportunity or requirement ID that resolves in its source file. Pass: 100% resolve. Fail: warn, and fix before build. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- As a named persona, I want a capability, so that a real benefit.
- No benefit clause, no story.
- Tasks are tasks — label them honestly.
- Split along the workflow, never along the layers.
- No criteria, no build.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every story passes the template lint (G-PR-041).
- [ ] Every role is a named persona or carries the all-segments reason (PR-082).
- [ ] Every benefit clause states an outcome, not the capability restated (PR-083).
- [ ] Technical work is labeled as tasks, not stories (PR-084).
- [ ] No story in build has zero acceptance criteria (G-PR-042).
- [ ] Oversized stories are split into whole-value pieces (G-PR-043).
- [ ] Every story traces to an opportunity or requirement ID (G-PR-044).
